# ASSURANCE-01 repository-wide audit

## Scope and evidence

This is the working investigation record for `ASSURANCE-01`. Its starting source is PR #302 at commit `42d02c5a38ecffaba59e58d5d56ba0ab858eda1f`. The audit covers the entire repository: product code, tests, fixtures, scripts, configuration, documentation checks, packaging, and CI. It is **incomplete**; the entries below are discoveries from successive source passes, not a conclusion that other areas are clear.

The [backlog matrix](backlog_matrix.md) owns the accepted outcome and task status. This document records evidence and questions. It authorizes no implementation, protection removal, coverage change, or evidence deletion. `QUAL-01` owns measured test cost; `HARNESS-01` owns simulated-science harness choices; `REPORT-ROSTER-01` owns the reporting roster decision.

All `path:line` references below refer to the pinned commit. **Source reviewed** means code or documentation was inspected, without execution in this audit. **Test characterized** means a committed test explicitly asserts the behavior; that test was not rerun for this record. **Inference** identifies a conclusion still needing a focused reproduction. No product or repository test suite, institutional Slurm run, scientific review, or biological validation was performed for this pass. Focused helper and tiny owner-path reproductions are identified in their entries; they do not execute a full Run or report transaction.

## Coverage ledger for the pinned tree

The pinned commit contains 575 tracked files. The counts below inventory every top-level surface; "sampled" means specific paths were inspected for the entries in this document, not that every file in a group has been cleared. The 53 route-level owner fault-map rows cover all twelve source surfaces, including both installed-provider boundaries. The active-file crosswalk and the schema/guide maps now account for all 315 tracked production paths by source-level role; this is a routing census, not a claim that every branch was individually cleared. The named test-file maps account for all 88 Python, ten shell, and two R `test_*` files by source-level fault family; they do not establish per-case sensitivity. File-by-file caller/fault disposition, focused proof of open cases, and any protection-retirement decision remain open.

These 53 owner rows cover supported entry routes and their first distinct fault comparisons across the twelve production surfaces. A final source-level comparison of analysis, orchestration/runtime, reporting, and artifact-contract owners added A01-455-458: descriptor metadata, a capacity rounding boundary, exact Step 10 final-path handoff, and the native shell receipt ceiling. Each has a different surviving defense and an explicit nonexecution limit. The active-file crosswalk below completes source-level routing for the remaining operational files. This closeout pass corrected Step 00a input/output roles, Step 04's index producer, Step 08/09 versus Step 10 publication order, Step 09's QC-summary continuity role, reference publication versus provenance pass, Run/Watch target selection, validator exit versus semantic all-pass, and guarded R startup. A01-475/476 record the remaining direct Watch root and child-count oracles; A01-477-480 record four direct-validator role-alias false passes without claiming the normal Run path reproduced them. No row clears a product file, test, script, schema, configuration entry, or gate for retirement. Exhaustive per-file branch/fault disposition and focused proof for the recorded gaps remain open; documentation, fixtures, scripts, configuration, packaging, and CI are repository-wide review surfaces beyond the production maps.

The reporting-start and verified-reporting schemas have similar shapes but protect different ledger transitions. The start record binds the origin and lock, while the verified record binds the start and semantic receipt (`src/emrys/contracts/schemas/orchestration/v1/reporting_start.schema.json:7-18,34-47`; `src/emrys/contracts/schemas/orchestration/v1/verified_reporting.schema.json:7-18,34-47`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/reporting_boundary.py:734-755,949-1026`). Direct ledger cases exercise both phases (`tests/contracts/orchestration/test_reporting_ledger_contracts.py:21-61`). Their similar field scaffolding alone does not establish a shared policy or justify removing either record.

The remaining six orchestration schema leaves also have active roles. `common` supplies shared identifiers and the distinct general/success command shapes (`src/emrys/contracts/schemas/orchestration/v1/common.schema.json:114-155`); `project` admits both the built-in flat analysis and module form, and shares reference STAR settings (`src/emrys/contracts/schemas/orchestration/v1/project.schema.json:37-46,60-132`; `src/emrys/contracts/schemas/orchestration/v1/reference.schema.json:27-49`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/normalization.py:596-638`). `resource-config` admits selected fragments before defaults merge and complete policy admission (`src/emrys/contracts/schemas/orchestration/v3/resource_config.schema.json:3-9`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/execution_profile.py:399-415`). `task-start` binds owner entry and inputs, while `verified-task` binds a later Task Attempt reference (`src/emrys/contracts/schemas/orchestration/v1/task_start.schema.json:7-20,50-65`; `src/emrys/contracts/schemas/orchestration/v1/verified_task.schema.json:7-17`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/task.py:2650-2665,2885-2920`). All six are registered and packaged (`src/emrys/contracts/orchestration/api.py:23-55`; `tests/test_package_distribution.py:61-79`). The two common command definitions share argv grammar but differ on permitted exits; that overlap alone does not establish a worthwhile reduction. No whole schema is cleared for retirement.

Two artifact-adapter cases would benefit from more precise diagnostics without changing the disposition of their current guards. Removing `SP` currently reaches the Step 07 required-definition check, and the test asserts its failed receipt and generic code (`tests/reporting/test_artifact_adapters.py:1538-1559`; `src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/reconcile_native.py:212-220`). Changing significant-row `qual` reaches Step 09's exact subset comparison, but the adapter test asserts only a failed summary (`tests/reporting/test_artifact_adapters.py:1622-1640`; `src/emrys/contracts/scientific_evidence/step09.py:751-760`). Pin each causal detail and sibling state if these cases are changed. The direct Step 09 contract test already matches the subset error (`tests/contracts/scientific_evidence/test_step09.py:345-358`); it does not prove adapter diagnostic propagation. Source order shows the current named-marker assertions remain sensitive to removal of their intended checks, unlike the masked fixtures in A01-442/445.

### Automated-gate crosswalk, source characterization

Four other definitions are manual or scheduled. Daily schedules select the Python 3.11 full suite and 130-pair synthetic Slurm profile; Sunday also selects the 100,000-pair profile. The pinned Ruff paths cover all 282 tracked Python/PYI files; `make lint` ShellChecks all 28 tracked shell files, whereas the optional pre-commit hooks check matching staged files (`scripts/make_quality.mk:7,228-236`; `.pre-commit-config.yaml:5-21`). Those timing and scope differences survive the shared tool names. The fixed Bash syntax roster omits the sourced production `argument_parsing.sh` and `file_checks.sh`; parsing a caller does not parse a sourced file. The all-file ShellCheck gate remains, so this is a standalone `smoke` scope limit, not a demonstrated ordinary-CI blind spot. No Make target or hook has been shown safe to remove.

A second source comparison of the Make recipes, CI job selection, hooks, and their tests found no additional whole-gate retirement candidate beyond the matrix entries. Staged-file lint, all-tracked-file lint, Bash syntax, installed-wheel smoke, behavioral shards, coverage finalization, guarded R, and synthetic Slurm exercise different inputs or evidence layers (`scripts/make_quality.mk:73-85,126-193,207-244`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml:164-420,901-1104`; `.pre-commit-config.yaml:1-21`). This is a source disposition, not a hosted result or a claim that every gate is complete.

## Discovery notes

### A01-01 — Step 07 selector validation false pass

**Supported behavior and failure.** Step 07's validation report should reconcile the declared region selector with the output transaction. `src/emrys/libraries/validation/mpileup.py:130-153` checks a region-file row for a known contig but does not establish its coordinate bounds. The owner emits this as `selector_reconciliation` in `src/emrys/stages/partitioned_cohort_mpileup/validator.py:138-150`. A retained test at `tests/stages/partitioned_cohort_mpileup/test_validate_step_07_mpileup_outputs.py:424-445` explicitly expects an all-pass report for a BED end beyond the FAI bound. The owner contract at `src/emrys/stages/partitioned_cohort_mpileup/CONTRACT.md:90-103` states a limited validator ceiling.

**Surviving defenses and next step.** Project admission and the producer check selectors before work; receipt and sample checks protect other properties. Those defenses do not establish that an existing Step 07 validation report proves selector bounds. Retain the characterization. Trace every consumer of this report, then decide the owner's required validation ceiling before proposing a fix.

**Caller trace.** Project admission and the producer reject out-of-FAI BED coordinates before normal Run work (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/onboarding.py:1631-1683`; `src/emrys/stages/partitioned_cohort_mpileup/producer.py:118-169`), and Run binds the selector as a stable input (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/materialization.py:742-755`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/task.py:2788-2800`). Reporting's native Step 07 reconciliation checks receipt/VCF relationships but not selector bounds or equality of `selector_type` and `selector_value` across its two receipt rows (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/reconcile_native.py:187-269`). The owner validator compares both rows with the partition manifest (`src/emrys/stages/partitioned_cohort_mpileup/validator.py:124-150`), and Run requires its all-pass report (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/task.py:2788-2800`). Adapter tests mutate record counts and header definitions, not a cross-orientation selector mismatch (`tests/reporting/test_artifact_adapters.py:1004-1025,1538-1565`). These are standalone report/index ceilings, not demonstrated supported-Run false passes. The report's intended selector claim still needs an owner decision.

### A01-02 — Selector syntax differs across owners

Project admission uses `str.isdigit()` before integer conversion (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/onboarding.py:1645-1651`); the Step 07 producer requires ASCII `[0-9]+` (`src/emrys/stages/partitioned_cohort_mpileup/producer.py:131-136`). `src/emrys/contracts/SOURCE_TOPOLOGY.md:45` records this disparity. An admitted Project selector therefore may not be accepted by the worker. This is a source-level mismatch, not a reproduced Run failure. Decide the supported coordinate syntax, inspect Project-side tests and all selector readers, and preserve producer refusal until caller-complete parity is demonstrated.

**Focused syntax probe.** Arabic-Indic `١` passes `str.isdigit()` and `int` but fails the producer's ASCII regex; superscript `²` passes `isdigit()` then raises raw `ValueError` in the Project helper. The producer test includes a superscript refusal (`tests/stages/partitioned_cohort_mpileup/test_partitioned_cohort_mpileup_producer.py:371-419`), but no Project Unicode fixture was found. This was not a full Project or Run invocation. A caller-complete grammar decision must preserve re-admission at each trust boundary.

### A01-03 — CI whitespace check does not inspect committed changes

`scripts/make_quality.mk:211-219` runs `git diff --check` inside `validation-static`. The CI job first checks out the commit and runs that target (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:173-185`); the command inspects unstaged worktree changes rather than the committed PR range. The local command remains useful for local edits. The checkout at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:118-122` does not request full history. Specify an event-aware committed comparison range, fetch enough history, and verify the file types before changing the gate.

**Focused reproduction.** In a disposable Git repository, a clean checkout with one committed trailing-space line returned exit 0 from `git diff --check`, while `git show --check HEAD` returned exit 2 and identified the line. This isolates the Git command's blind spot; it is not a hosted CI run with a bad commit. Keep the useful local check and choose a committed comparison range with sufficient event-specific checkout history.

**CI event scope.** The workflow invokes the static target for pull requests, master pushes, merge groups, and selected manual dispatches (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:3-18,164-186`). Its shared checkout has no explicit history depth (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:118-122`). Workflow and Make tests protect trigger/target wiring but do not inject a bad committed line (`tests/test_ci_workflow.py:65-69,111-131`; `tests/test_validation_orchestrator.py:101-133`). The bare check also serves useful local invocation paths (`tests/tools/run_validation.py:154-164`). Define the checked result and comparison endpoints separately for PR, merge-group, push, and manual events; fetch or validate both endpoints and fail clearly when a required endpoint is absent. A net two-tree diff and every-intermediate-commit scan make different promises. The disposable Git reproduction supports the command-level failure; no hosted bad-commit run was performed.

**Local staged scope.** A fully staged trailing-space line also escapes bare `git diff --check`: in a second disposable repository probe, the bare command returned 0 while `git diff --cached --check` returned 2 for the staged file. Local contributor guidance calls for quick checks before committing (`AGENTS.md:27-33`), so the current local target has a staged-file blind spot as well as the hosted committed-range blind spot. Keep the unstaged check where useful; define staged and event-specific committed comparisons as separate gates. This probe did not run Make or CI.

### A01-04 — Validation inventory assertion misses source owners

`tests/contract_integration/validation_rosters/test_validation_check_rosters.py:84-95` says it checks the exact live validator inventory, but scans `scripts/validate_step_*.py`. The listed validators reside under `src/emrys`; the scan and its expected script subset are both empty at this commit. The test still confirms that its named paths exist and that its two lists agree. The companion test guide's claim to cover every current producer inventory (`tests/contract_integration/validation_rosters/README.md:3-6`) therefore needs the same scope qualification: literal rosters cover report-producing owners, while the vacuous script scan does not discover a new source-owned validator. The gap is discovery of a *new* source-owned validator, not loss of every roster check. The Stage Map identifies 14 built-in stage, evidence, and analysis owners (`src/emrys/contracts/STAGE_MAP.md:17-34`), while the grouped CLI exposes 17 validation routes including three generic commands (`src/emrys/__main__.py:11-33,44-65`). Literal check-ID expectations cover Steps 00a–09 (`tests/contract_integration/validation_rosters/validation_roster_expectations.py:5-102`), and Step 10 has a direct one-row assertion (`tests/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/scientific_context_projection/test_validator.py:80-99`). Profile-to-Stage Map and template checks are separate surviving defenses (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_profile.py:271-306`). Reconcile the owner identity, installed route, and emitted-report sets without adding another mutable product registry; preserve literal oracles independent of producer constants.

The pinned tree has 16 source-owned `validator.py` modules: the 14 Stage Map owners plus the standalone manifest and artifact-contract validators. All 16 are imported into the grouped CLI's 17-route `_VALIDATION_OWNERS` table; `all-pass` supplies the remaining route (`src/emrys/__main__.py:11-65,318-334`). The literal roster table is intentionally limited to the 14 report-producing owners, while the owner suites invoke `assert_exact_check_roster` against completed reports (`tests/contract_integration/validation_rosters/validation_roster_expectations.py:5-114`; `tests/stages/star_index/test_validate_step_00a_star_index.py:108`; `tests/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/test_validate_step_09_cmh_outputs.py:223`). A replacement inventory check should derive the 16 modules from the source tree, compare them with actual public route modules, and separately compare the 14 report producers with the Stage Map and literal rosters. This is a static source/route mapping, not an executed discovery test or evidence that a current owner is missing. The public CLI contract test exercises its listed routes but does not discover an added validator route (`tests/test_public_cli_contracts.py:37-64`). Step 10 currently asserts one passing row without asserting the emitted check ID (`tests/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/scientific_context_projection/test_validator.py:80-99`); its positive oracle must be added before treating the 14-owner roster comparison as complete. The `REPORT_LIBRARY` path constant is assigned once and never used by any tracked caller (`tests/contract_integration/validation_rosters/test_validation_check_rosters.py:14-17`); removing that line is a separate test-only cleanup. Replacing the empty `scripts` scan with real source discovery would also make `SCRIPTS_ROOT` unnecessary, but the stronger inventory comparison must be designed before deleting the old lines.

### A01-05 — Central roster mutation multiplication

The contract-integration file parametrizes generic roster mutations across its listed steps (`tests/contract_integration/validation_rosters/test_validation_check_rosters.py:98-146`). The shared report validator has no step-specific branch (`src/emrys/libraries/validation/report.py:83-111`). There are 56 literal-oracle variants (one Step 10 reorder skips) and 56 shared-helper variants: 42 missing, extra, or appended-duplicate refusals and 14 reorder acceptances. All 42 negatives change row count and stop before ID-set comparison (`src/emrys/libraries/validation/report.py:97-106`). The current duplicate mutation appends the first ID, so it does not test equal-count duplicate refusal (`tests/contract_integration/validation_rosters/test_validation_check_rosters.py:72-80`). Reordering the one-check Step 10 roster leaves it unchanged. The existing library test separately rejects an equal-count wrong ID (`tests/libraries/test_validation_report.py:161-168`). A tiny source-bound `validate_report` probe with two expected IDs refused missing, unique extra, and appended-duplicate rows at the count gate, refused an equal-count duplicate at the ID-set gate, and accepted reordering. An isolated AST copy of that exact function with only the count guard removed still rejected missing, unique extra, and equal-count duplicate rows at the ID-set gate but **accepted the appended duplicate**. This proves a distinct count-only witness; it did not execute an owner CLI, test suite, or supported Run.

A conditional **five-case** shared-report set would use a singleton missing row, a multi-check appended unique ID, a multi-check appended duplicate ID, an equal-count duplicate *replacing* one expected ID, and a meaningful multi-check reorder. The first three should pin the `exactly N checks` diagnostic; the appended duplicate is the unique current count-guard witness when the ID set is unchanged. The replacement duplicate should pin `check IDs are invalid` and reach the set guard. Reorder characterizes present acceptance, a defect ceiling rather than supported behavior to preserve indefinitely. Reducing 56 shared-helper variants to five would remove 51 collected and executable pytest nodes. A four-case set without the appended duplicate would lose count-guard fault sensitivity, as the isolated mutant showed.

The separate literal-oracle test mutates the same table it reads and calls one generic tuple comparison (`tests/contract_integration/validation_rosters/test_validation_check_rosters.py:98-114`; `tests/contract_integration/validation_rosters/validation_roster_expectations.py:105-116`). It does not run an owner validator or independently detect a wrong literal table value. Source searches found exact emitted-report roster assertions in the thirteen Step 00a–09 owner suites; Step 10's direct success test does not assert its emitted check ID (`tests/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/scientific_context_projection/test_validator.py:40-100`), as A01-331 records. Four representative literal-helper mutations could replace its 56 variants only after A01-04's live-owner inventory is repaired and Step 10 has a positive emitted-roster oracle. That cut would remove 52 collected nodes but 51 executable cases because the current one-check Step 10 reorder is skipped. It would lose per-owner negative witnesses and step-specific mismatch-diagnostic checks; preserve the fourteen literal expectation tuples, each owner success assertion, and four literal-helper cases: missing, unique extra, equal-count wrong ID, and meaningful reorder. An appended duplicate is another length mismatch for this tuple comparison; its distinct count-guard fault is retained in the shared-report case above.

Together the revised conditional cuts could remove 103 collected nodes and 102 executable cases. The shard baseline's unlisted-node 1.0-second value is a scheduling estimate, not observed cost (`tests/baselines/python_test_durations.json:1-9`; `tests/tools/python_test_shards.py:150-155`). Retain the independent wrong-ID library case (`tests/libraries/test_validation_report.py:161-168`) and reporting's distinct malformed-roster checks (`tests/reporting/test_artifact_adapters.py:559-604`). This is a source/test comparison. Only the isolated AST count-guard mutant probe ran; no reduced suite, owner report, or CI run was executed in this audit pass.

### A01-06 — Canonical document names and headings

`scripts/documentation/validate_structure.py:14-34,199-206` requires 19 named documents and an H1 somewhere in each. These pages include durable scientist, operator, architecture, owner, and accepted-work homes assigned by the documentation authority map (`docs/design/decisions/repository-and-delivery.md:79-89`). A named-path check can detect removal of an authority page even if its inbound link is also removed; local-link admission checks a different stale-destination fault (`scripts/documentation/validate_structure.py:164-196`). `first_heading` (`:120-126`) accepts any nonempty H1 text, regardless of position. `tests/documentation/test_validate_structure.py:158-176` explicitly accepts a renamed Workflow title. Thus the gate protects page presence and minimum heading structure, not title identity or first-line placement. The test fixture mirrors the 19 names at `tests/documentation/test_validate_structure.py:17-37`, but its negative test (`:179-195`) exercises only Workflow, Runbook, and Troubleshooting. Sixteen required names have no negative case or assertion binding the fixture roster to the product roster. Removing one of those sixteen names from `CANONICAL_DOCUMENTS` would leave the synthetic fixture present and its existing diagnostics unchanged. The real-tree gate would remain green while that page still exists; if the page and its inbound links were later removed together, link validation would not restore the fixed-page promise. This is a source counterfactual, not a mutated test run or a currently missing document. Compare the product roster with the independent literal 19-path fixture and keep the three missing/unheaded behavior cases. ### A01-07 — Anchor parser and tilde fences

Local link targets and anchors are checked in `scripts/documentation/validate_structure.py:164-196`. Its anchor extractor (`:129-147`) toggles fenced-code state only for backticks, although CommonMark also permits tilde fences. A heading-looking line inside a tilde fence could therefore satisfy a link to a nonexistent heading. An isolated local call to `markdown_anchors` on a temporary file containing only a tilde fence and `# phantom` returned `phantom` as an anchor. This does not establish the full documentation check's behavior under every input.

The same extractor recognizes only unindented raw ATX lines and slugs raw source text (`scripts/documentation/validate_structure.py:129-147`). CommonMark setext headings, ATX headings indented one to three spaces, and rendered text from an inline-link heading are outside that model. A valid `#title` link could be rejected, while a source-derived non-rendered slug such as `#titleguidemd` could be accepted (`:164-196`). The direct link test covers a plain anchor and a missing anchor, not these heading forms (`tests/documentation/test_validate_structure.py:290-310`). Its valid `#runbook` anchor is placed beside two intentional link errors; the assertions require the intended errors but never rule out an extra false-rejection of that valid anchor (`:295-310`). The first run does separately exclude a diagnostic naming the valid `guide(1).md` target (`:306`), so that particular acceptance is partly protected. After the bad links are removed, a Mermaid fault still prevents the fixture from asserting a clean link result (`:312-323`). This is source inference about future syntax or regression, not a broken tracked link. Reuse one established Markdown parse/slug contract for anchors, and isolate a successful anchor/link fixture while retaining destination existence and containment checks.

Raw HTML `<a href>` and `<img src>` targets are also outside `markdown_destinations`, which selects only MarkdownIt `link_open` and `image` children (`scripts/documentation/validate_structure.py:150-160`). The documentation-checker guide calls its scope local links and anchors (`scripts/documentation/README.md:4-7`), but no pinned tracked raw-HTML link/image attribute was found. Decide whether such HTML is prohibited or included before expanding the gate; preserve ordinary Markdown link checks. The tilde-fence probe remains the only executed case in this entry.

Guarded real-R tests assert literal candidate order and worker-count byte determinism (`tests/stages/cohort_candidate_preprocessing/test_step_08_vcf_preprocessing.R:619-635,873-885`). Retain both evidence layers; a passing Python report alone does not prove the producer's scientific reconstruction.

**Downstream trace.** Reporting's Step 08 native reconciliation checks source bindings, sample order, partition/orientation counts, and summary arithmetic, but does not reconstruct candidate IDs or row order (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/reconcile_native.py:271-435`). Its TSV adapter records header and row-count evidence for Step 08 sites (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/_text_tabular.py:19-111`). The Step 09 owner compares its carried rows with the Step 08 rows it reads (`src/emrys/contracts/scientific_evidence/step09.py:804-832`), while reporting's Step 09 projection binds Step 08 source path/hash and sample order (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/reconcile_step09.py:37-72`). These downstream consistency checks do not independently establish Step 08 candidate ID/order derivation. No full report falsification fixture was run; retain guarded real-R literal and determinism oracles.

**Standalone coordinate ceiling.** The shared Step 08 sites helper parses genomic `position` as nonnegative (`src/emrys/contracts/scientific_evidence/step08.py:520-522`), and the owner report checks positive positions only when `--step07-root` is supplied (`src/emrys/stages/cohort_candidate_preprocessing/validator.py:189-195`). A tiny coherent sites/receipt helper fixture accepted `position=0`; no full owner report was run for that fixture. The runner does supply `--step07-root` (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/materialization.py:798-810`), so this does not establish a normal Run false pass. Direct owner tests characterize arbitrary IDs and row order, not zero position (`tests/stages/cohort_candidate_preprocessing/test_validate_step_08_preprocessing_outputs.py:376-390`). Decide whether standalone inspection promises VCF-valid coordinate bounds or only carried transaction structure before changing the optional-context boundary.

**Carried VCF-field ceiling.** The Step 08 sites header carries source QUAL, FILTER, and INFO alternate depth, and the R worker fills them from its VCF reader (`src/emrys/stages/cohort_candidate_preprocessing/step_08_vcf_preprocessing.R:19-25`; `src/emrys/stages/cohort_candidate_preprocessing/_step_08_vcf_processing.R:227-230`; `src/emrys/stages/cohort_candidate_preprocessing/CONTRACT.md:53-57`). The shared Python sites validator does not inspect the three values after header admission (`src/emrys/contracts/scientific_evidence/step08.py:483-584`). Its direct negative fixtures exercise position, flags, and sample counts/frequencies, while guarded R asserts some INFO depth values but no independent QUAL/FILTER source comparison (`tests/contracts/scientific_evidence/test_step08.py:501-520,620-655`; `tests/stages/cohort_candidate_preprocessing/test_step_08_vcf_preprocessing.R:648-668`). Step 09 carries this metadata and checks agreement with the Step 08 table, not the VCF's original values (`src/emrys/contracts/scientific_evidence/step09.py:438-486,804-832`); reporting reconciles source hashes, header IDs, sample order, and counts but not those cells (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/reconcile_native.py:187-435`). Thus a standalone coherent table can carry lexically malformed QUAL or negative INFO depth without a site-helper refusal. The owner contract limits the Python check to basic/table-internal fields (`src/emrys/stages/cohort_candidate_preprocessing/CONTRACT.md:92-99,121-129`), so decide whether stronger direct admission is promised before adding those oracles. This source trace is not evidence that normal R emits such values.

### A01-22 — Step 09 validation does not recompute CMH statistics

`tests/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/test_validate_step_09_cmh_outputs.py:282-335` fabricates CMH statistics, p-values, adjusted values, and odds ratios while the report passes. `src/emrys/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/CONTRACT.md:105-113` states this ceiling. A production-independent Python oracle and guarded R corpus cover numerical behavior (`tests/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/test_step_09_cmh_oracle.py:108-178`; `tests/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/test_step_09_cmh_editing_site_calling.R:222-313`). Preserve the characterization and independent oracles, and avoid promoting report status to scientific proof.

**Corpus-maintenance ceiling.** The Step 09 boundary-coverage test unions free-text `requirement_tags` from the corpus rather than deriving categories from the input count vectors or expected results (`tests/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/test_step_09_cmh_oracle.py:126-146`). Tags could drift onto ordinary rows while that breadth assertion still passes. The committed corpus currently contains the named difficult cases, and per-case independent Python and guarded R checks compare numeric outputs (`tests/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/step_09_cmh_oracle.tsv:2-13`; `tests/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/test_step_09_cmh_oracle.py:149-178`; `tests/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/test_step_09_cmh_editing_site_calling.R:239-313`). This is a future fixture-maintenance weakness, not evidence that today's numerical oracle is vacuous. Preserve the corpus and independent calculations if deriving coverage from values later.

**Synthetic end-to-end ceiling.** The generated fixture declares expected control/treatment allele frequencies, a positive difference, and common odds ratio (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/synthetic_fixture.py:627-640`), but the real-tool E2E Step 09 oracle reads only candidate ID and call status, checks three/all and one/significant rows, and never compares those numeric expectations (`tests/tools/real_synthetic_e2e.py:872-910`). It accepts either `significant_up` or `significant_down` for the selected candidate despite that declared positive direction (`:900-904`). Its successful result would not independently detect an internally consistent wrong effect size or direction in that hosted journey. The numerical corpus and guarded R tests above protect different inputs and computations; Run receipts protect byte identity.

In particular, the guarded R test executes the committed CMH implementation against every literal corpus row and checks its integrated fixture's ordering, statuses, summary, directional cases, and global BH values (`tests/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/test_step_09_cmh_editing_site_calling.R:157-313,586-678,806-955`). A01-22 concerns arbitrary externally supplied, internally consistent values at direct report admission, not absence of a normal native-computation oracle. Decide whether the synthetic E2E promises the fixture's literal effects before adding a justified numeric assertion and requiring the expected `significant_up` direction. A01-183 separately concerns status vocabulary and cross-file agreement in this direct driver oracle. No hosted run or full-Run false pass was reproduced in this audit.

### A01-30 — Scheduler fixture case multiplication

The current submission writer emits v4 requests (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/control.py:1175-1194`), while retained-request admission recognizes v1–v4 and observation intentionally requires complete v2–v4 request-specific streams (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/slurm_submission.py:55-59,95-105,219-245`). Older-version fixtures therefore exercise a supported retained-diagnostic path; a newer writer alone does not make them obsolete. The reduction question is repeated case combinations, not wholesale legacy-reader removal.

`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_slurm_submission.py:1482-1609` expands three request versions, three cluster arrangements, and four states into 36 cases around shared observation logic. The request observer distinguishes unnamed v2 from named v3/v4, while the scheduler observer branches on cluster selection, live versus accounting response, terminality, and usage (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/slurm_submission.py:219-245`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/scheduler_observation.py:94-299,351-425`). The contract specifies local matching-root `sstat` for live usage, recorded-cluster `sacct` for terminal usage, and preservation of root state when usage is unavailable (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/CONTRACT.md:592-602`). In the fixture, PENDING and CANCELLED issue one root query; local RUNNING issues four queries including `sstat` and root rechecks; remote RUNNING issues two without `sstat`; COMPLETED issues seven including `sacct` root/batch and rechecks. The full product therefore makes 111 fake scheduler calls. A source-level 12-case pairwise cover uses C0 = no recorded cluster/local alpha, C1 = recorded alpha/local alpha, and C2 = recorded alpha/local beta:

| Version | PENDING | RUNNING | COMPLETED | CANCELLED |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v2 | C2 | C0 | C1 | C0 |
| v3 | C1 | C2 | C0 | C1 |
| v4 | C0 | C1 | C2 | C2 |

Every version/state, cluster/state, and version/cluster pair remains in the 12-case subset, including local live `sstat`, remote live usage refusal, and a completed `sacct` path. Its only remote-live RUNNING case is v3/C2; it omits v2/C2/RUNNING on the unnamed retained-reader path and v4/C2/RUNNING on the current named-request path. `_observe_batch_usage` rechecks the root before and after batch usage (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/scheduler_observation.py:351-425`); a fault restricted to an omitted version/cluster/state interaction could survive the subset. The proposed cut would remove 24 collected cases and reduce expected fake scheduler calls from 111 to 37, with elapsed saving unmeasured. Adding the two omitted remote-live cases would yield 14 cases and 41 calls, still without proven equal fault sensitivity. All CANCELLED cells in this fixture receive their root from `squeue`; only COMPLETED exercises positive accounting usage. Bind A01-394's exact root selector on every query and compare focused faults and cost before any reduction. Preserve adjacent identity-drift, malformed live/terminal usage, and date-order tests (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_slurm_submission.py:1611-1771`).

The named-request cases have a separate query-format oracle gap. Their fake `reply` always adds `JobName` to the returned root row for v3/v4, regardless of whether the `squeue` or `sacct` argv requested that field (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_slurm_submission.py:1503-1540`). The assertions check the resource-field suffix and resulting `job_name`, not the `|,Name:0` or `,JobName` selector itself (`:1546-1563`). An isolated source-bound AST copy removed those two format tokens while preserving the parser's expected fields; the same fake still yielded accepted RUNNING and COMPLETED observations with complete usage after four and seven calls, respectively. This demonstrates test insensitivity to a lost name-field request, not a real Slurm result or a present source defect. Make the fake return only requested fields or assert the name selector on every named root query before using this matrix as scheduler-format proof. A01-394 separately covers exact root `-j` selectors.

A separate request-specific-stream roundtrip repeats three commands over v2/v3/v4, nine cases (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_slurm_submission.py:881-935`). Stream and scheduler-name policy vary by schema, while command-specific admission distinguishes `run` from a request with `requested_run` (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/slurm_submission.py:122-165,171-195`). The adjacent resume/report exact-Run test starts from `_request_record`'s default v1 (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_slurm_submission.py:60-67,863-878`), so it does not replace the nine-case matrix's v4 resume/report positives. Moreover, that matrix changes `command` and `requested_run` but leaves `emrys_argv` as `run` (`:88-98,887-895`); A01-444 traces the resulting coherence gap. Its v2/v3 cases take a current v4 plan and replace only name/stream fields (`:892-913`), so they are synthetic retained-reader records rather than historical producer roundtrips. Repair command/argv coherence and retain coherent v4 resume/report cases before evaluating a possible five-case set of v2/v3/v4 `run` plus v4 resume/report. Keep the negative stream/name cases at `:937-976`; neither five-case fault sensitivity nor elapsed saving is established.

The invalid-request observation test multiplies three retained-record defects by `include_resources=False/True` (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_slurm_submission.py:979-1001`). All three start from `_request_record`'s default v1 (`:60-67`), which `observe_submission_request` refuses even if a partial or unconfirmed record-status check regresses (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/slurm_submission.py:219-245`). The two status variants therefore do not independently prove their intended guard. First use a current v4 or supported v2 request for partial and unconfirmed transcripts, assert the exact `record_status` and no scheduler query, and keep a complete v1 legacy case. A partial current-version record with a confirmed job ID isolates the status guard; unconfirmed still has no ID, so its refusal has an overlapping identity defense. Only then compare one `include_resources` value per defect against the six current variants; the option is not read before refusal. Valid resource observation remains covered by later scheduler cases. These are fixture-repair and conditional test-reduction steps, not a present scheduler fault.

### A01-31 — Scheduler response cap is after capture

`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/scheduler_observation.py:54-68,208-218` captures subprocess stdout before rejecting replies over 64 KiB. The coordinator contract (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/CONTRACT.md:487-496`) acknowledges that capture memory is not strictly bounded. Oversized-byte tests (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_slurm_submission.py:1922-1956`) protect admission of a reply, not process-memory bounds. Retain that defense and do not report it as a bounded capture proof.

The submission transport has a separate live/retained bound: ordinary `submit` reads all retained `sbatch.stdout` into memory, and waited mode reads an unbounded first line and remainder before constructing diagnostic text (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/slurm_submission.py:1005-1059`). `_submitted_response` accepts a canonical job ID plus any nonempty cluster string on its sole line (`:1095-1111`), whereas the later request reader caps `sbatch.stdout` at 4,096 bytes and marks an overlong response's job ID unconfirmed (`:577-600`). A malformed one-line `ID;cluster` response with a very long cluster name could therefore be announced as submitted (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/control.py:1206-1225`) yet lose exact retained job observation. Existing ordinary-response tests use small bytes (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_slurm_submission.py:1369-1479`); no realistic Slurm client is shown to emit the malformed value, and no fake-client or cluster submission was executed for this note. Raw transcripts survive, and the duplicate-submission guard treats unknown prior observation conservatively (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/control.py:1113-1164`). Compare accepted live grammar, retained reader bounds, and transcript memory before changing either boundary; do not infer a lost Run or automatic duplicate submission.

Removing the group itself is a caller-complete migration: update the default-group list, ten CI flags, three operator commands, the literal configuration assertion (`tests/test_validation_orchestrator.py:60-89`), and the lock in one approved slice. The historical quickstart/Doctor alignment note (`docs/tasks/polish-campaign.md:379-388`) also needs interpretation before changing the user-facing command. ### A01-73 — Saved settings can block diagnostic CLI flags

The public entry point loads a saved `.env` from the current directory or an ancestor before it parses any arguments (`src/emrys/__main__.py:349-373`). There is a separate availability ceiling before `main`: the module eagerly imports functional owners (`src/emrys/__main__.py:11-33`), then parses version/help only inside `main` (`:349-373`). A source-bound local `python3 -m emrys --version` stopped at an absent declared `jsonschema` dependency during import, before dispatch. If version/help are intended for diagnosing a damaged environment, test that promise separately from the consuming-command dependency contract.

Thus following the tracked sample can silently leave intended defaults unapplied and then block supported setup; it does not demonstrate a Run or execution-profile bypass. No full CLI sequence was run. Decide whether to retire this stale sample or replace its guidance with the current closed setup contract; preserve create-absent behavior and avoid deleting operator data.

The shared Step 08 scientific-evidence parser accepts any-length ASCII decimal with a regex, then calls Python `int` (`src/emrys/contracts/scientific_evidence/step08.py:195-198`). Step 08 and Step 09 validators use this parser for input/summary counts (`src/emrys/stages/cohort_candidate_preprocessing/validator.py:99-102,205-208`; `src/emrys/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/validator.py:140-149,251-254`); Step 10 scientific context also calls it (`src/emrys/contracts/scientific_evidence/scientific_context.py:409-417`). The shared validation CLI runtime does not catch `ValueError` (`src/emrys/libraries/validation/runtime.py:14,63-72`). Reporting has a separate regex-then-`int` native-field reader (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/reconcile_native.py:33-39`), while its per-scope reconciliation catches only `ArtifactIndexError` (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/reconciliation.py:72-88`); that reporting consequence is source inference because its full import was unavailable locally. Ordinary numeric tests cover valid and short invalid forms (`tests/contracts/scientific_evidence/test_step08.py:378-413`). Preserve the distinct scientific-evidence and reporting trust boundaries while normalizing bounded decimal conversion.

The same conversion ceiling reaches two other owner inputs. Step 02b's flagstat parser matches any-length ASCII counts, then converts without a `ValueError` guard (`src/emrys/libraries/evidence/qc.py:8-33`); a focused 5,000-digit total raised raw `ValueError` before its validator could build a failed report (`src/emrys/evidence/canonical_bam_qc/validator.py:54-68`). Step 07 region parsing likewise converts an unbounded numeric match (`src/emrys/libraries/validation/mpileup.py:98-125`); a focused `selector_ok` call with `chr1:` followed by 5,000 digits escaped its `ValidationError` catch (`:130-141`). Project setup and Project admission also catch only that controlled error around the same parser (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/onboarding.py:1063-1067,1739-1746`). These probes do not execute full owner commands or prove normal tool output can contain such values; they extend the malformed-input fault map without merging the distinct evidence and Project boundaries.

An adjacent reporting input has a different conversion failure: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is parsed as an integer with a controlled `ValueError`, but an integer outside the platform timestamp range can raise raw `OverflowError` at `datetime.fromtimestamp` (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/core.py:57-69`). A temporary standard-library probe with a 29-digit integer reproduced that exception; the artifact-index builder calls this helper at both start and finish (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/context.py:164,189`). Committed reporting fixtures set an ordinary fixed epoch (`tests/reporting/test_artifact_adapters.py:119-147,701`). This is a malformed environment diagnostic, not an artifact-index false pass or a claim about a normal Run. Preserve deterministic timestamps while defining the representable epoch range and controlled error type.

The orchestration contract JSON loader has the same diagnostic shape at a different authority boundary. It converts admitted bytes with `json.loads` but catches `UnicodeError` and `JSONDecodeError`, not the `ValueError` raised by Python's integer-string limit (`src/emrys/contracts/orchestration/api.py:124-138`). On local Python 3.14.5 with its default 4,300-digit limit, a standard-library parse of a JSON object containing a 5,000-digit integer raised raw `ValueError`. The artifact-contract JSON loader has an independent copy of that error boundary. It catches `UnicodeError` and `JSONDecodeError` but not `ValueError` around `json.loads` (`src/emrys/contracts/artifacts/_artifact_contracts/schema.py:40-52`). An isolated extraction of the pinned loader functions admitted a ten-digit numeric field and raised raw `ValueError` for a 5,000-digit value. Storage qualification has the same malformed-JSON-number diagnostic gap at its own evidence boundary. `_json_object` catches decode and syntax errors, but Python's 4,300-digit integer limit raises `ValueError` for a 5,000-digit JSON integer (`src/emrys/evidence/storage_inventory/qualification.py:330-337`). ### A01-77 — Valid Step 06 rounded fraction can fail validation

The Step 06 producer writes `assigned_records/input_records` with Python `:.6f` (`src/emrys/stages/mechanical_orientation/producer.py:140-169`). The owner validator compares the parsed float to the unrounded ratio with a strict `<= 0.0000005` tolerance (`src/emrys/stages/mechanical_orientation/validator.py:103-114`). For valid counts `input=2,000,000` and `assigned=800,003`, the exact rational ratio is halfway between `0.400001` and `0.400002`; the observed producer value is `0.400002`, while binary-float subtraction is `5.000000000143778e-7`. The assigned arithmetic check failed in a tiny direct validator fixture. Reporting uses `5.000001e-7` for the same producer format (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/reconcile_native.py:175-183`), although its comment calls that Python formatting `printf`. Run requires semantic all-pass (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/task.py:2763-2807`), so the supported-Run impact is source-composed inference, not a completed Run reproduction. Retain exact count arithmetic; decide whether admission means an inclusive exact rational/decimal half-quantum window or the precise producer-formatted numeric value, then align owner validator and reporter. At this tie, both six-decimal neighbors `0.400001` and `0.400002` differ from the exact ratio by `5.000000000143778e-7` in binary float and fail the owner, while longer nonproducer `0.4000015` and `4.000015e-1` pass. Simply copying the reporter epsilon admits both adjacent values and does not prove exact producer formatting. This was a tiny arithmetic probe, not an owner or Run execution for each spelling.

The existing positive producer and owner fixtures use exactly representable six-decimal ratios, while the owner negative changes multiple count relationships together (`tests/stages/mechanical_orientation/test_mechanical_orientation_producer.py:123-137`; `tests/stages/mechanical_orientation/test_validate_step_06_orientation_outputs.py:38-55,113-127,143-175`). The reporting six-decimal fixture uses a zero reverse group, which the actual producer refuses (`tests/reporting/test_artifact_adapters.py:1591-1619`; `src/emrys/stages/mechanical_orientation/producer.py:150-153`). A caller-complete parity case can use input 2,000,000; flags 99/147/83/163 of 200,000/200,001/200,000/200,002; FWD-like 400,001; REV-like 400,002; assigned 800,003; and unassigned 1,199,997. It should assert the literal producer fraction `0.400002`, require all five owner rows and the reporting artifact to pass, then change only the fraction outside the admitted window and require refusal. This protects the boundary without weakening the separate count equalities.

### A01-81 — PID existence is weaker than Run owner identity

After lock/Attempt binding and host checks, local Run inspection calls `process_is_alive` and labels a true result `local live owner` (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/inspection.py:298-353`). That helper uses only `os.kill(pid, 0)` and treats `PermissionError` as alive (`src/emrys/libraries/process_environment.py:55-64`); the Attempt and projected Run lock bind host and PID but no process-start identity (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/materialization.py:1473-1507`; `src/emrys/contracts/orchestration/api.py:191-205`). If the original process dies and the host reuses its PID, inspection can label the unrelated process as the lock owner and set `running` (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/inspection.py:440-451`). Existing tests inject live/dead Boolean responses, not PID reuse (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_lifecycle.py:3575-3635`). This is source inference, not a reproduced live PID reuse. If the reused PID is treated as a live origin, inspection passes `allow_incomplete_origin` into Task evidence (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/inspection.py:486-500`), suppressing missing Task terminal/start blockers and the missing latest terminal-receipt blocker (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/_inspection_attempts.py:459-463`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/_inspection_evidence.py:239-243`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/inspection.py:513-520`). Define the needed process identity evidence or state the observable liveness limit.

### A01-84 — Isolated child tests do not prove package identity

The Matplotlib determinism test starts two `sys.executable -I -c` children from unrelated temporary directories, imports `emrys.reporting...figures`, and compares figure hashes and environment state without recording `figures.__file__` or another source identity (`tests/reporting/test_figures.py:198-279`). Isolated Python ignores the parent's `PYTHONPATH`; a local source-bound test can therefore fail if no package is installed or probe a stale installed package if one exists. Hosted CI first synchronizes the locked project environment (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:919-933`), and same-process figure tests still exercise their selected import, so this does not establish a hosted CI false pass. The installed logging-delegate smoke similarly invokes `sys.executable -I -c`, skips when the child reports no installed `emrys`, and asserts event order and stream separation without recording the imported package's path or revision (`tests/libraries/application_logging/test_installed_smoke.py:13-87`). The full public-CLI suite has a separate parent/child package-path comparison (`tests/test_public_cli_contracts.py:713-734`), and hosted full-suite shards first synchronize the locked project (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:919-933`). Those are surviving defenses, so this is a standalone/subset identity ceiling rather than a demonstrated complete-CI false pass. Retain the logging event-order and stream assertions and bind the child when claiming coverage of the checked-out revision.

The same isolated-child attribution question applies to Step 02b and Step 03 validator CLI tests: their helpers invoke `sys.executable -I -m emrys` from arbitrary working directories and compare owner reports, while their parent tests import checkout modules (`tests/evidence/canonical_bam_qc/test_validate_step_02b_bam_qc.py:12-13,73-92,141-175`; `tests/evidence/rseqc_orientation/test_validate_step_03_rseqc_orientation.py:12-13,65-84,150-183`). ### A01-101 — Report receipt can exceed the CSV field limit

The report receipt writer repeats the entire canonical JSON document in one TSV field for each HTML output (`src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/receipt.py:157-185`). Fresh publication re-reads its staged receipt before linking final outputs (`src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/publication.py:154-164`; `src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/validation.py:58-79`), so this ceiling predicts a controlled publication refusal rather than false evidence admission. The exact canonical JSON, receipt equality check, input hashes, and receipt-last publication remain useful. Decide a format or bounded-reader policy at this owner without globally changing Python's CSV limit or silently truncating provenance; compare actual provider input sizes before assigning operational priority.

The built-in paired-CMH module declares seven Step 09 and six Step 10 artifacts (`src/emrys/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/__init__.py:129-176`). Its reporter combines a fixed set of Step 09 tables/manifest and Step 10 tables/bound inputs, deduplicated by path before core adds the remaining declared artifacts (`src/emrys/reporting/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking_report/computational.py:86-101`; `src/emrys/reporting/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking_report/scientific_context.py:41-57,95-102`; `src/emrys/reporting/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking_report/provider.py:115-133`; `src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/context.py:253-292`). The 1,000-input probe is therefore not a built-in Step 09/10 roster. The installed collaborator reporter interface permits a returned input tuple without an explicit count cap (`src/emrys/reporting/__init__.py:57-78`); receipt construction repeats that admitted roster in canonical JSON (`src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/receipt.py:89-100,157-185`). Keep this as an extensible-provider format ceiling, with no measured built-in receipt size or external-provider run.

### A01-102 — Build metadata can be paired with another package tree

`admit_installed_package` hashes bytes under the executing `PACKAGE_ROOT` but selects build provenance separately by the distribution name `emrys-rna-workflow`; it checks metadata shape and re-reads it but does not verify that the selected distribution owns that import root (`src/emrys/libraries/source_authority.py:21-23,68-125`). A tiny isolated source-bound fixture ran the actual function with the pinned checkout as the executing package tree and a temporary unrelated distribution metadata directory on `sys.path`. `importlib.metadata.distribution()` selected that directory, and admission returned its invented version, Git commit, and lock hash alongside a real digest of the checkout's package bytes. This was an unusual import/metadata split, not the normal controlled installed-wheel command; no scientific execution bytes were forged.

The distinction matters to attribution: the reporting contract says installed-code hash, version, and build provenance enter the manifest and receipt (`src/emrys/reporting/README.md:51-58`), and report context and receipt carry the selected `git_commit` and package record (`src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/context.py:386-417,458-469`; `src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/receipt.py:120-125`). Existing source-authority tests change a temporary `PACKAGE_ROOT` while retaining ambient distribution metadata and check byte-change sensitivity and malformed metadata, not distribution ownership (`tests/libraries/test_source_authority.py:123-170`). The controlled Python startup and isolated-wheel test establish separate defenses against adjacent source loading (`src/emrys/libraries/source_authority.py:146-173`; `tests/test_package_distribution.py:341-362`); they do not prove the general metadata/root pairing. Preserve the exact content digest, symlink refusal, and repeated admission while defining which distribution file ownership or install-path evidence can support the Git/version attribution.

### A01-107 — CI selection assertions check tokens, not job conditions

The pinned workflow gives `workflow-lint` and eight other ordinary jobs conditions that run automatically on ordinary events and require a selected input on manual dispatch (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:109-115`; `tests/test_ci_workflow.py:25-35`). The workflow contract test checks each condition for three substrings: non-dispatch, non-schedule, and its input name (`tests/test_ci_workflow.py:111-117`). Appending a valid `|| true` to a job condition would retain all three substrings and pass this assertion while also selecting that job on unselected manual dispatches and schedules. This is a regression-test ceiling; the pinned workflow source itself expresses the intended condition, and no workflow was altered or run for this probe.

The workflow-lint source test checks that the intended Actionlint ignore token appears, but does not pin it as the only ignore or require failure to remain fatal (`tests/test_ci_workflow.py:897-901`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml:155-162`). A broader ignore, an appended shell success clause, or continue-on-error could leave that test green. The current step has none of those bypasses; checksum-verified Actionlint installation and hosted lint remain distinct live defenses (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:141-153`). Pin the complete lint command and failure propagation alongside the job-selection checks. This is a future-regression oracle gap, not a current lint bypass or hosted result.

Actionlint checks syntax and embedded shell, not the intended event truth table (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:155-162`). The same test pins a nine-job selection mapping and manual input roster (`tests/test_ci_workflow.py:25-35,73-108`), which protect different drift but do not establish the truth value of each `if`. Retain those checks and compare conditions by exact semantics or a small event/input truth table before claiming that scheduled and manual lane selection are protected.

Failure propagation is another CI-test ceiling: the static/docs/wheel job puts its checks in one step, and the contract test pins that step's script lines but does not reject a future `continue-on-error: true` on the step (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:164-186`; `tests/test_ci_workflow.py:120-134`). That mutation would preserve the script and Actionlint syntax while making a failing step nonfatal to the job. The synthetic E2E lane demonstrates a stronger local pattern for intentional `continue-on-error`: it inspects selected step outcomes before claiming success (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:1275-1299,1385-1417`; `tests/test_ci_workflow.py:786-829`). Current static-wheel has no bypass, and no CI run or mutation was performed. Preserve the actual failure gate when improving its contract test.

Within that synthetic final gate, the current workflow correctly requires both selected profile uploads, checkout preservation, and the infrastructure upload in addition to profile execution (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:1385-1417`). The focused contract test asserts the two profile-run outcomes appear in the final environment and that the script mentions `UPLOAD_INFRASTRUCTURE`, but does not require `UPLOAD_130`, `UPLOAD_100000`, or `CHECKOUT_OUTCOME` in the failing condition (`tests/test_ci_workflow.py:785-820`). Dropping one of those dependencies could leave this source test and syntax lint green. This is a test-regression ceiling, not a current bypass or hosted result. Extend the final-gate test to the complete selected outcome graph without removing the current upload and checkout gates.

**Long-run concurrency.** The current group selects `github.run_id` for scheduled/manual events and the cancellation policy excludes those events (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:58-60`). Its focused test checks only that the group string contains the schedule condition, dispatch condition, and run ID, while asserting the cancellation expression exactly (`tests/test_ci_workflow.py:137-147`). A valid group expression that selects nonempty `github.ref` first would retain those three tokens but group separate long runs by ref, permitting unintended collision. This is a future-regression test ceiling, not current cancellation. Pin a small event/ref/run-ID truth table or exact intended expression while preserving the existing cancellation assertion.

**Manual guard binding.** The manual-selection test asserts the eight environment *names* and error phrase, but not each environment value or condition operand (`tests/test_ci_workflow.py:73-108`). The pinned workflow maps all eight inputs correctly (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:84-107`). If `RUN_SYNTHETIC_100000` were accidentally bound to `inputs.synthetic_130`, a 100000-only dispatch would fail the at-least-one-lane guard although the synthetic job selects `inputs.synthetic_100000` independently (`:1099-1104`); the current source test and syntax lint could remain green. Add exact input-to-guard mapping and condition-operand assertions alongside the existing roster and job-selection checks. No dispatch or CI run was made.

**Manual refusal exit.** The same source test checks the guard's input names and diagnostic phrase but not its failure status (`tests/test_ci_workflow.py:73-108`). Removing only `exit 2` from the all-false branch would leave the tested text and valid shell intact (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:84-107`); every ordinary and synthetic lane can then skip an unselected manual dispatch (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:109-114,166-169,903-905,1099-1104`), leaving a misleading successful run. Keep the guard and require a nonzero all-false result plus a selected-lane success in a focused contract oracle. This is a hypothetical source-regression path, not a changed workflow or executed dispatch.

**Python shard result binding.** Both aggregate jobs run under `always()` and download selection receipts that shards upload under `if: always()` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:936-991,1055-1097`). The receipt verifier proves complete and disjoint selected node IDs, not that those tests passed (`tests/tools/python_test_shards.py:299-357`). The current workflow therefore has a separate `Require every ... shard to pass` step for both Python versions, testing the respective `needs` result for `success` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:980-981,1096-1097`). The direct 3.11 workflow test checks receipt upload/download and verifier arguments, but no source test pins either aggregate job's `needs` link and successful-shard step (`tests/test_ci_workflow.py:904-933`). If a success step disappeared, valid selection receipts could still let a failed shard yield a misleading green aggregate, especially in the 3.11 lane without a coverage floor. Pin both dependency/result gates while retaining the selection verifier and hosted execution as distinct evidence. The workflow is currently guarded; this is a source-test ceiling, not an observed failed CI run.

**Minimum Python job binding.** The ordinary compatibility job sets up Python 3.11, compiles the tracked Python trees, runs the isolated wheel test through `validation-wheel-smoke`, and invokes the example manifest command (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:70-75,993-1021`; `scripts/make_quality.mk:83-85`). These protect syntax, installed distribution, and public input admission on the minimum interpreter; the scheduled behavioral sharder excludes the wheel test (`tests/tools/python_test_shards.py:20-23`). The workflow-source test checks the minimum job's condition and only the `compileall` fragment of its command; no test pins `MINIMUM_PYTHON_VERSION` or the setup action's version binding (`tests/test_ci_workflow.py:111-117,288-292`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml:70,1003-1007`). Removing the wheel or manifest invocation, or drifting the configured interpreter above 3.11, could leave those source assertions green while ordinary CI loses that specific minimum-version check; the primary-version static-wheel job would still protect a different interpreter. Pin the version binding, three intended phases, and their failure propagation without adding a duplicate nightly lane. This is a future-regression test ceiling, not an observed CI omission or hosted result.

**Primary-version and final policy-step binding.** The workflow sets `PRIMARY_PYTHON_VERSION` to `3.14`, and the primary setup alias reads that value before the Python 3.14 shard and aggregate jobs (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:70-73,124-129,901-914,948-960`). No tracked workflow test pins that value or alias binding (`tests/test_ci_workflow.py:25-35,279-286`). The aggregate currently runs `make -s python-coverage-enforce` after receipt verification, successful-shard admission, and coverage finalization (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:974-991`); the Make target enforces the reviewed baseline (`scripts/make_quality.mk:184-187`). The workflow test checks shard worker/thread fragments but contains no assertion for this final policy invocation (`tests/test_ci_workflow.py:279-286`). Removing that step could leave complete receipts and successful shards while dropping global and critical-owner coverage enforcement; changing the primary version could leave a job labeled Python 3.14 on another interpreter. Pin both source bindings and failure propagation. The current workflow retains them; no hosted job or coverage measurement was run for this finding.

A further isolated workflow-condition probe wrapped each current scheduled Python 3.11 full-job expression in parentheses and appended `&& false`. The two exact substring assertions at `tests/test_ci_workflow.py:150-157` still passed, while both modified conditions were unsatisfiable, disabling scheduled behavioral shards and their aggregate (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:1023-1027,1064-1070`). The ordinary 3.11 smoke cannot replace that suite: it checks compileall, an installed wheel, and an example manifest, while full-shard collection excludes the wheel test (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:993-1097`; `tests/tools/python_test_shards.py:20-23,93-98`). The primary static lane runs under Python 3.14, a different interpreter boundary (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:70-75,164-186`). Pin an event/input truth table for the scheduled pair. This was a source-bound in-memory condition probe, not a hosted run or a whole-gate retirement case.

### A01-109 — A competing selector can strand the admitted predecessor

The shared `publish_exclusive(..., replace_expected=...)` path opens and checks the old bytes, renames the old name to a displaced sibling, then links the staged replacement to the original name (`src/emrys/libraries/exclusive_publication.py:64-104`). If another process creates the original name between the rename and the link, the `FileExistsError` branch unlinks the displaced old file before refusing the replacement (`:103-109`). A tiny direct helper fixture inserted a competing `runtime.tsv` at that exact link seam: the call raised its controlled replacement error and retained the competitor, but the previously admitted `old selection` bytes no longer existed at any path in the temporary directory. This did not run a supported Doctor operation or a real concurrent process.

Doctor uses this replacement path to move a dependent Project's selected shared-runtime generation after separately qualifying the candidate (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/doctor.py:1830-1873`). Its owner guide says replacement requires the same source Project, the exact prior selector, fresh probes, and a maintenance claim, while retained Runs keep their old selector (`src/emrys/evidence/runtime_availability/README.md:75-95`). The existing helper test injects a competing change *before* the rename and proves the competitor survives; it does not exercise a competing creation after the rename (`tests/libraries/test_exclusive_publication.py:44-69`). Preserve no-clobber, old-byte admission, staged fsync, and competing-file refusal, but retain the displaced predecessor for inspection or recovery when this later race occurs. ### A01-110 — Duplicate HTML attributes can hide active style and DOM identity

The rendered-report inspector receives an ordered list of attributes from Python's `HTMLParser`, then converts it to `dict`, keeping the last value of any repeated name (`src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/validation.py:210-216`). It stores that map for `<main>` and compares `data-report-view`, `data-run-id`, and other provenance fields with the expected identity (`:243-246,457-475`). It also passes only the mapped `style` value to its embedded-CSS check (`:285-292`). A standard-library probe with first `data-run-id="foreign"` and `style="background:url(https://example.invalid/a)"`, followed by second values `data-run-id="expected"` and `style="color:black"`, retained both pairs but exposed only the second values in the map. The [HTML Standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#attribute-name-state) specifies that a browser discards later duplicate attributes, leaving the first values in the DOM. The inspector's separate active-resource loop reads every original pair but does not inspect inline `style` there (`:293-314`; `src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/models.py:25-42`). The same bytes can therefore have a first-value browser style containing a non-embedded URL while the static CSS check sees only the benign second value, as well as a different DOM provenance identity. This is source composition plus a parser probe, not a completed report transaction or observed installed-template output.

The current provider-markup tests mutate active resources and event attributes but do not challenge duplicate provenance or style names (`tests/reporting/test_report.py:480-512`), and the installed template is not shown to generate duplicates. Required banner, one-main, per-pair event and URI checks, exact output-byte, receipt, and post-publication rechecks remain separate defenses (`src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/validation.py:293-314,370-475`; `src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/publication.py:154-180`). Reject duplicate HTML attributes before semantic checks, rather than trusting the last-value map. No browser network request was observed in this audit.

The shared `parse_header` helper requires one `@HD` line and one `@RG` line, then tests whether the expected `SO:coordinate`, `ID:<scope>`, and `SM:<scope>` tokens occur among each line's tab-separated fields (`src/emrys/libraries/alignments/bam.py:56-65`). Steps 02, 04, and 05 use the shared result to mark their coordinate-sort and read-group report checks (`src/emrys/stages/canonical_bam/validator.py:60-69,105-116`; `src/emrys/stages/duplicate_marking/validator.py:60-67,96-100`; `src/emrys/stages/split_n_cigar/validator.py:88-96,127-131`). ### A01-112 — Escaped CSS functions evade report resource scans

The core report validator searches CSS text for literal `url(` and `@import` patterns (`src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/models.py:47-50`; `src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/validation.py:126-133`). The scientific SVG validator similarly searches literal `url(` and `@import` in style text and attributes (`src/emrys/reporting/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking_report/figures.py:187-204`); an isolated extraction of that pinned function accepted the escaped form while refusing the literal form. The [CSS Syntax Level 3 specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-syntax-3/#consume-an-ident-like-token) consumes escapes into an identifier before recognizing a case-insensitive `url` function.

External scientific-provider markup reaches the core rendered-report check (`src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/context.py:226-250`; `src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/publication.py:154-180`). Tests reject literal remote CSS and active markup, but do not exercise escaped function names (`tests/reporting/test_report.py:480-509`; `tests/reporting/test_figures.py:691-702`). No tracked built-in CSS or figure is shown to emit this escape, and no completed report, browser fetch, or network request was observed. This is a separate parsing mechanism from A01-95's omitted SVG resource attribute and A01-110's duplicate HTML attributes. Define one CSS grammar and refusal rule across both rendering boundaries; preserve output-byte, receipt, and post-publication identity checks.

The SVG negative fixture combines `@import` and literal `url(https://...)` in one style element, then asserts only a generic refusal (`tests/reporting/test_figures.py:691-702`). In the current branch, the `@import` condition rejects first, so removal of the style-URL check would leave this case green (`src/emrys/reporting/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking_report/figures.py:187-193`). The separate attribute-URL check has no focused negative in that test matrix (`:194-204`). Isolate style-URL without `@import`, `@import` without `url(`, and a URL-bearing attribute; retain script, external href, and XML-base refusals. This is a masked source-level test oracle, separate from the escaped-CSS parser bypass.

### A01-113 — Parent replacement can misbind a stable text snapshot

`stable_text` takes a no-symlink child snapshot, reads through `Path.read_text`, and compares the child snapshot again (`src/emrys/libraries/validation/inputs.py:27-55`). The pathname read is not bound to the inode observed in either snapshot. In a tiny temporary fixture, the original `admitted/source.tsv` contained `safe`, while an alternate directory held a same-name symlink to `false-pass`. Replacing only the parent directory during `Path.read_text` and restoring it before the second snapshot made the actual helper return `false-pass\n` with the unchanged original five-byte snapshot; the path afterward again read `safe\n`. A direct child-file swap was rejected in an earlier probe because its ctime changed. This is a deliberately timed same-user filesystem race, not a reproduced owner report or normal Run.

Several owner validators consume that helper, including STAR index and alignment logs, Step 04 metrics, Step 07 selector and VCF, and RSeQC text (`src/emrys/stages/star_index/validator.py:116-129`; `src/emrys/stages/star_alignment/validator.py:63-76`; `src/emrys/stages/duplicate_marking/validator.py:68-70`; `src/emrys/libraries/validation/mpileup.py:142-160`; `src/emrys/evidence/rseqc_orientation/validator.py:55-64`). The `stable_text` test checks a changed before/after snapshot (`tests/libraries/test_validation_report.py:114-141`). Separate descriptor-bound byte readers have mutation and replacement tests (`src/emrys/libraries/validation/inputs.py:58-76`; `tests/libraries/test_validation_inputs.py:210-312`), so this is a specific text-reader identity gap, not an absence of input protection across the library. Audit each caller's size and UTF-8 policy before reusing a descriptor-bound read; preserve exact errors, snapshot meaning, and report publication rechecks.

### A01-114 — Scientific completion sentence survives unavailable Step 09 sources

The scientific HTML template always says that its view reports the "completed Step 09 analysis" when `scientific` is true (`src/emrys/reporting/templates/run_report.html.j2:174`). Condition the sentence on admitted computational evidence, or explicitly distinguish completed execution from unavailable evidence. The test was characterized from source and was not rerun in this audit.

### A01-115 — Non-UTF-8 reference predecessor escapes controlled reconciliation

When all three reference-provenance outputs already exist, publication reads each prior output and passes it to `validate_output` before replacing anything (`src/emrys/evidence/reference_provenance/reconciler.py:76-89`). That validator decodes bytes without handling `UnicodeDecodeError` (`src/emrys/evidence/reference_provenance/reconciler.py:39-49`).
