The `finally` block still removes its own lock (`src/emrys/evidence/reference_provenance/reconciler.py:114-120`); the observed failure is loss of controlled malformed-predecessor diagnosis, not a false provenance pass or a reproduced Run failure. Existing owner fixtures exercise partial predecessor, foreign lock, and replacement rollback, but not this complete malformed predecessor (`tests/evidence/reference_provenance/test_reference_provenance.py:371-389,430-518`). Preserve the three-output rollback behavior while converting prior-output decoding to the owner error contract.

### A01-116 — Step 10 direct contract can admit changed output bytes

The shared scientific-context transaction first calls `_bound_path` for each receipt-declared file, requiring its current SHA-256 to equal the recorded hash (`src/emrys/contracts/scientific_evidence/scientific_context.py:981-995,1346-1369`). It later reopens the four outputs for semantic admission and computes each returned `ContextTable.sha256`, but compares only row counts with the receipt before returning success (`src/emrys/contracts/scientific_evidence/scientific_context.py:327-328,1377-1408`). A tiny temporary owner fixture changed the candidate-context TSV from LF to CRLF immediately after `_bound_path` returned; the rows retained their meanings. The actual `validate_scientific_context_transaction` returned success while the receipt hash differed from current output bytes and the returned table hash matched the changed bytes. The committed stale-output test mutates before admission, not between those reads (`tests/contracts/scientific_evidence/test_scientific_context.py:155-176`). This is a deterministic direct-contract check/use gap, not proof of a live filesystem race or completed Run false pass.

The Step 10 validation CLI snapshots all declared files and rechecks them before publishing an executed report (`src/emrys/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/scientific_context_projection/validator.py:92-110`; `src/emrys/libraries/validation/runtime.py:27-47`). Reporting also compares the returned output-table hash with its own artifact snapshot (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/reconcile_step10.py:22-43,85-105`). Those surviving boundaries limit this finding; a size-changing LF-to-CRLF mutation would be caught on those paths. Reconcile the semantic reader's exact bytes with the receipt inside the shared contract without removing the CLI/report checks or the independent reference-window oracle.

### A01-117 — Direct Step 08 validator can publish after upstream change

With `--step07-root`, the Step 08 validator reopens each exact Step 07 receipt and VCF, comparing its hash and declared identity with the Step 08 input table (`src/emrys/stages/cohort_candidate_preprocessing/validator.py:45-94`). This is a direct-validator transaction continuity gap, not evidence that a supported Run completed with changed upstream input.

The direct mutation test covers each of the six returned snapshots after report construction (`tests/stages/cohort_candidate_preprocessing/test_validate_step_08_preprocessing_outputs.py:307-354`). Another test changes a Step 07 receipt or VCF between separate validator invocations and observes a failed reconciliation on the second call (`:420-459`); neither covers the post-reconciliation interval. Keep that Run boundary and the existing six-input publication checks while extending the direct validator's exact upstream snapshot set when `--step07-root` is supplied.

### A01-119 — Guided Project inspection does not establish paired FASTQ identity

Named Project creation invokes sample admission with `inspect_fastqs=True`, then rechecks input snapshots before publishing the Project (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/onboarding.py:1329-1353,1374-1391`). The streaming inspector parses record framing, sequence/quality lengths, and a maximum read length independently for each file; it does not retain read names for comparison (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/normalization.py:157-226`). `_normalize_samples` inspects each mate and retains its snapshot but never compares their record counts or IDs (`:345-412`). An existing plain/gzip test deliberately admits one R1 record named `@r1` and two R2 records named `@first` and `@later` (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_onboarding.py:1296-1307`). This is a characterized admission ceiling and a source-composed guided-creation path, not an executed full `emrys init` fixture with that pair.

The owner contract promises each FASTQ's record inspection during creation (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/CONTRACT.md:184-198`). Normal Run forwards the admitted mate paths to STAR; its worker checks file presence, compression mode, and native output, while its validator checks BAM and STAR logs rather than pairing (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/materialization.py:513-547`; `src/emrys/stages/star_alignment/step_01_star_align.sh:55-77`; `src/emrys/stages/star_alignment/validator.py:45-118`). The Step 01 contract explicitly limits what byte stability and suffix checks prove (`src/emrys/stages/star_alignment/CONTRACT.md:27-42`). An optional diagnostic compares four-line block counts and a requested prefix of normalized read IDs, but is outside the normal Run graph (`src/emrys/ingestion/sample_manifest_admission/README.md:10-13,29-32`; `src/emrys/ingestion/sample_manifest_admission/check_fastq_pairs.sh:114-170`). That prefix is not a whole-file ID proof.

The same guided scanner checks only the first header byte and can count a complete record whose header is just `@` (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/normalization.py:193-222`); direct guided tests cover truncation, length, gzip, and long-line cases but not an empty read identifier (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_onboarding.py:1296-1394`). This is a source-inferred header-grammar question, distinct from mate-to-mate identity comparison; no native STAR behavior is claimed. Decide whether Project readiness requires early count or ID matching and a nonempty identifier, then adjust the accepted input and cost policy across creation and hand-authored admission; otherwise make the current per-file promise explicit. No native STAR outcome, supported-Run completion, or biological pairing was established here.

The optional operator-run pair checker has a narrower but misleading same-file route. It verifies each path is a file and compares counts and normalized prefix IDs without checking that R1 and R2 denote distinct files (`src/emrys/ingestion/sample_manifest_admission/check_fastq_pairs.sh:91-101,114-170`). In a disposable local fixture, one valid one-record FASTQ supplied as both `--r1-fastq` and `--r2-fastq` returned zero and printed `PASS: FASTQ pair check succeeded`; the positive direct tests supply distinct paths (`tests/ingestion/sample_manifest_admission/test_check_fastq_pairs.py:90-137`). Project admission separately rejects identical authored mate paths (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/normalization.py:378-386`), and the helper guide explicitly disclaims complete pairing and provenance (`src/emrys/ingestion/sample_manifest_admission/README.md:10-18`). Decide whether the advisory command's paired-file claim should refuse identical files, including aliases, or state this limit in its output. Preserve its count, prefix, decompression, and no-write checks. The tiny fixture establishes only the optional helper's response, not Project or Run admission.

### A01-121 — Task can publish verified marker after a late input change

The Task binds initial stable-input size/hash records, then compares those inputs with fresh snapshots after producer, validator, and semantic checks (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/task.py:2600-2616,2788-2792`). `_publish_attempt` embeds the original input rows in a succeeded terminal record, publishes it, and revalidates logs (`:2378-2439,2865-2882`). Before publishing the verified marker, Task rechecks reused and ordinary outputs, input-directory membership, the validation report, and its terminal record, but does not rehash ordinary stable-input files (`:2889-2924`). Thus an input changing at the terminal-record publication interval could leave a direct Task invocation with a verified marker bound to the old input hash. A same-length byte replacement would evade a file-size or path-only recheck. This is a source-composed interval, not a reproduced Task or complete-Run false pass; the audit Python lacks the owner fixture dependencies, and none were installed.

Existing Task tests mutate an input during producer execution and replace a Step 00c output at terminal-record publication; they protect distinct early-input and late-output failures but not the late-input interval (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_task.py:2178-2191,3066-3099`). Retained `validate_verified_task` does rehash each recorded input/output (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/task.py:2265-2277`), and Run lifecycle re-inspects task evidence after workflow completion and blocks success on integrity failures (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/_inspection_evidence.py:118-150`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/lifecycle.py:2020-2059`). Preserve that later boundary. Decide the direct Task marker's continuity promise and recheck stable input files immediately before its publication if the marker must be truthful on its own.

The existing `_task_fixture` declares a normal `owner_input` and no input directories (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_task.py:101-103,140-158`). Its `_observe` wrapper can run a callback after the real terminal `publish_bytes` call, as the late-output test already does (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_task.py:209-220,3066-3099`). Change `built.mutable_input` to different bytes of the same length in that callback and require a controlled Task refusal with no verified marker. This isolates ordinary input-content continuity from directory-member and late-output checks. No such fixture was executed in this audit.

### A01-122 — Step 10 Fisher rederivation accepts a materially false effect and p-value

The Step 10 contract promises Fisher's conditional odds-ratio estimate, exact two-sided 95% interval, and two-sided p-value for its one inferential row (`src/emrys/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/scientific_context_projection/CONTRACT.md:51-59`). R computes them with `stats::fisher.test`; Python independently rederives a conditional distribution from the admitted counts (`src/emrys/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/scientific_context_projection/scientific_context_projection.R:670-684,703-721`; `src/emrys/contracts/scientific_evidence/scientific_context.py:481-574,649-719`). Python compares odds and interval bounds on a reciprocal root scale with absolute tolerance about `0.000122`, and compares p-values with a general absolute tolerance `1.5e-8` (`src/emrys/contracts/scientific_evidence/scientific_context.py:124-125,577-589,693-719`; `src/emrys/contracts/scientific_evidence/step08.py:217-220`). These absolute tolerances become broad when a valid odds ratio is large or a valid p-value is very small.

A tiny 400-row output fixture used the repository's synthetic context builders for an informative table with 199 of 200 foreground candidates and 1 of 200 background candidates carrying the motif (`tests/scientific_context_test_support.py:53-103,127-298`). Base R's `stats::fisher.test` returned conditional odds about `15447`, interval about `[2101, 4.5e15]`, and p about `7.77e-115`. The exact `validate_scientific_context_outputs` path admitted those R values. Changing only the reported odds ratio to `1000000` and p-value to `0` still passed the output validator; all other context, hit, logo, and statistics rows stayed fixed. The incorrect odds ratio is about 65 times R's value, and zero is not the computed p-value. This is a small output-owner semantic false pass, not a forged receipt, completed Run, or biological interpretation. Production R and receipt/hash checks remain separate defenses against ordinary output corruption.

The committed output helper hardcodes a positive Fisher oracle only for the 10/20 population with 5/2 motif hits; the guarded real-R fixture and contract mutation tests use that same informative table (`tests/scientific_context_test_support.py:219-263,326-344`; `tests/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/scientific_context_projection/test_real_r_projection.py:125-129,181-197,287-338`; `tests/contracts/scientific_evidence/test_scientific_context.py:82-132`). The existing corpus thus protects one ordinary effect, while zero-cell and stronger or alternate informative cases have no independent positive golden. Preserve the conditional recomputation, exact payload/receipt binding, and real-R comparison; add scale-aware numerical acceptance and representative independent count/effect fixtures after the owner defines justified R/Python numerical behavior. This is distinct from A01-22's Step 09 CMH report ceiling.

### A01-136 — Generic report-output uniqueness checks may be redundant

The report-receipt schema requires exactly two outputs (`src/emrys/contracts/schemas/artifacts/v5/report_receipt.schema.json:146`). Semantic admission first checks unique IDs, kinds, and paths, then requires the exact ordered pair of output IDs and checks each ID's distinct required kind and basename in one directory (`src/emrys/contracts/artifacts/_artifact_contracts/report_receipt.py:42-86`). Both production entry points shown in this repository validate the schema before semantics (`src/emrys/contracts/artifacts/validator.py:47-62`; `src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/receipt.py:28-43`). Even a direct semantic call cannot admit duplicate IDs: the later ordered tuple has exactly two distinct required IDs. Distinct per-ID required kinds reject duplicate kinds, and distinct required basenames in one publication directory reject duplicate paths. The early checks therefore add earlier, more specific diagnostics rather than a distinct refusal.

A direct negative fixture appends a third duplicate-kind output and pins that diagnostic while bypassing schema-first admission (`tests/contracts/artifacts/test_artifact_schema_contracts.py:158-164,439-446`). The three early checks occupy seven physical lines plus an import name that becomes unused if they go. A further five-line set-of-output-IDs check is dominated by the immediately following exact ordered tuple comparison even for a direct semantic call (`src/emrys/contracts/artifacts/_artifact_contracts/report_receipt.py:50-65`). It adds a different wrong-ID diagnostic, pinned by a schema-valid direct test (`tests/contracts/artifacts/test_artifact_schema_contracts.py:448-451`), but no distinct refusal. No tracked assertion pins the early duplicate-path message.

An isolated standard-library probe loaded the pinned semantic function and compiled an AST copy with those twelve guard lines omitted. Across 1,885 generated output combinations, the original and mutant had zero acceptance differences; first-error messages changed. This direct-call probe did not execute schema validation, full publication, retained transaction re-admission, or an external caller. The ratified reporting decision explicitly requires future changes to retain error messages (`docs/design/decisions/execution-evidence-and-reporting.md:186-192`). Thus the proposed twelve-line reduction is blocked by the current promise, not merely pending a convenient test update. It would need an approved revision of that diagnostic promise plus a replacement oracle before implementation. Preserve schema-first admission, exact output mapping, direct refusal, and staged/final receipt readmission (`src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/receipt.py:143,188-217`; `src/emrys/reporting/transaction_validation.py:520-522`). No report or CI run was performed.

### A01-186 — Step 00c worker parses each sidecar twice in one phase

The candidate removes the two one-use wrappers, puts their checks immediately before their corresponding captured parses, and saves 15 physical product lines and two AWK launches per successful or mismatched worker. Nine exact-function cases matched exit status, stdout, and stderr byte for byte; a full scratch copy of the candidate also passed shell syntax and the existing fake-tool worker suite with its configured SHA-256 Python. The committed suite has no malformed FAI, malformed DICT, or pair-mismatch negative (`tests/stages/fasta_sidecars/test_step_00c_prepare_gatk_reference.sh:175-194`). The fixture changed ordinary files at fixed paths, not symlinks; no supported Run or external concurrent process was used.

### A01-189 — One-hit Step 10 fixture hides the nearest-bin counting distinction

The shared scientific-context fixture inserts at most one `TGTACA` motif per hit-bearing candidate and computes each position bin's `candidate_with_motif_count` from the same `hits_in_bin` value as `hit_count` (`tests/scientific_context_test_support.py:99-103,271-289,326-344`). Production's policy is different for a multi-hit candidate: the R producer counts every motif hit in `hit_count` but counts the candidate once in the bin of its nearest hit, breaking equal-distance ties by leftmost start; Python admission reconstructs that same distinction (`src/emrys/analyses/paired_cmh_candidate_ranking/scientific_context_projection/scientific_context_projection.R:659-667,750-772`; `src/emrys/contracts/scientific_evidence/scientific_context.py:788-813,910-933`). With a 201-base context centered at offset 100 and separated motifs beginning at positions 90 and 105, the two hits occupy bins `-10` and `0`; each bin has one hit, but only bin `-10` has one candidate under the tie rule. The current shared builder would assign one candidate to both bins, so it cannot provide that discriminating positive result without revision.

This is a source-inferred fixture/oracle ceiling, not a demonstrated current R or Python miscount. Add one literal two-hit positive case that pins both hit counts, the one nearest-candidate count, and tie behavior, while retaining the existing one-hit corpus, real-R projection, and independent Python admission. A01-187 separately limits the expanded Step 09 statistical family used by that real-R fixture.

### A01-194 — Oversized PDF startxref aborts artifact-index preflight

The PDF adapter requires a version header and terminal `startxref`/EOF, but its regular expression accepts an unbounded decimal offset from a tail of up to 65,536 bytes and calls bare `int()` on it (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/binary_readers.py:221-246`). Under the local Python 3.14.5 default decimal-conversion limit of 4,300 digits, a tiny standard-library check confirmed that a 5,000-digit offset raises `ValueError`. Context preparation has no per-row exception boundary (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/context.py:172-179`).

The existing binary negative fixture checks only truncated/signature PDFs and expects a failed artifact row (`tests/reporting/test_artifact_adapters.py:1562-1588`). Add one well-formed header with a 5,000-digit terminal offset and require the PDF's `adapter_validation_failed` row, preserving other artifact rows and the whole-operation error catch for genuinely unclassifiable failures. The digit-limit behavior depends on the executing Python setting; the package supports Python 3.11+ (`pyproject.toml:12`). No full builder or Run was executed with this input.

### A01-202 — Empty Python shard selection invokes default discovery

The shard planner accepts any positive shard count and allocates one list per shard, so a count above collected behavioral node IDs leaves empty selections (`tests/tools/python_test_shards.py:56-63,130-166`). `run_shard` records the empty plan, then passes it to `pytest_command`; that command appends no positional node IDs and therefore invokes Pytest's default test discovery (`:199-214,241-285`). An empty shard could thus run default discovery, potentially including those excluded tests, while its receipt claims zero selected tests. The command wrapper passes these arguments to `pytest.main` in the ordinary in-process path (`tests/tools/python_test_shards.py:217-230`).

Direct shard tests use nonempty 3-node/2-shard and 8-node/2-shard plans (`tests/test_python_test_shards.py:47-94,126-168`), while pinned CI configures four shards for a much larger suite (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:70-74,901-911,1023-1034`). Preserve complete/disjoint receipt verification and per-shard success gates. Reject a count that creates empty selections or handle empty shards as explicit no-ops before invoking Pytest, and test the exact command and receipt together.

### A01-203 — Real-engine DAG oracle loses concrete scopes

The public Run owner-double fixture has the related input-to-output ceiling: it builds all processing and analysis output payloads from a fixture projection before execution and replaces each producer/validator command with a payload publisher (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/fixtures/b5_doubles.py:29-70,83-123`; `tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/fixtures/task_double.py:87-96`). ### A01-205 — Direct R restoration admits ambient mutable paths

The direct `make r-restore` target requires a nonempty existing `RENV_PROJECT`, then invokes the guarded profile without setting `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY` or `RENV_PATHS_CACHE` (`scripts/make_quality.mk:92-100`). Thus an external Project alone does not establish that every mutable renv location stays external. This is a source-inferred direct-operator path risk, not a reproduced package write.

The Runbook instructs operators to set external Project, library, and cache paths together (`docs/operations/RUNBOOK.md:736-751`), CI sets all three beneath its temporary root (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:220-226`), and Doctor builds a managed location (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/doctor.py:1223-1232`). The direct shell fixture checks its Make selector and external Project but not inherited library/cache values; its R profile fixture checks project/lock/state/staging, not those two effective paths (`tests/shell/test_local_r_environment.sh:160-188,225-269`). Preserve those documented and managed guards. Decide the direct restore policy, then test the effective renv library/cache locations with an isolated safe fixture before claiming installed-package protection for arbitrary operator environments.

### A01-234 — Shared descriptor-reader faults are multiplied across output modes

Four parametrized negatives inject open failure, in-place mutation, post-open pathname replacement, and final pathname-metadata change into three readers, producing 12 collected cases (`tests/libraries/test_validation_inputs.py:25-42,210-312`). All reach `_read_file`, but the wrappers return full bytes, a bounded four-byte prefix, or a streamed digest (`src/emrys/libraries/validation/inputs.py:58-90,142-211`). Full bytes feed validation and Task records, prefixes feed BAM/BAI signatures, and digests bind Task/runtime inputs (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/all_pass.py:77-79`; `src/emrys/libraries/alignments/bam.py:15-29,68-73`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/task.py:565-583`). The mutation fixture rewrites a seven-byte file with 15 bytes after its first read (`tests/libraries/test_validation_inputs.py:229-248`). Full-byte and digest readers can reject on observed-size mismatch even without identity comparison; the bounded prefix stops after four expected bytes, so it uniquely isolates during-read identity from size mismatch among these current cases. A tiny source-bound same-size mutation from `fixture` to `mutated`, with forced mtime drift, refused all three modes: full-byte and digest reads took seven bytes then EOF, and prefix read four. The post-open replacement fixture also remains red if the first pathname check is bypassed, because the final check catches it after a read (`src/emrys/libraries/validation/inputs.py:175,196-197,224-236`; `tests/libraries/test_validation_inputs.py:251-283`). That does not protect the first guard's no-read boundary, especially when digest reading uses an `observe` callback. The current `_read_sha256` wrapper does not pass an observer (`tests/libraries/test_validation_inputs.py:25-42`); make the retained early-replacement case call `sha256_with_identity` directly with one, then assert zero reads and an empty observer before refusal (`src/emrys/libraries/validation/inputs.py:75-89`).

The final pathname-metadata fixture changes mode to `0o600` on the second `os.stat` (`tests/libraries/test_validation_inputs.py:286-312`). If the first path check disappears, the mutation is never triggered and this test can accept; that is a brittle indirect call-count witness. Under a restrictive umask the starting mode might already be `0o600`, so capture and flip one mode bit deterministically. This same-inode change can also fail the descriptor before/after identity comparison (`src/emrys/libraries/validation/inputs.py:196-210`), so it does not isolate the final pathname guard. To protect that guard, replace the pathname only after the initial check, from an `os.read` seam, while leaving the open descriptor and returned bytes stable; final path binding should then be the reason for refusal (`src/emrys/libraries/validation/inputs.py:175,196-197,224-236`).

A conditional seven-case basis would retain one open failure, same-size mutations in all three modes, an early replacement in direct digest mode with no-read/empty-observer assertions, a deterministic mode-change case, and a late pathname replacement. It preserves the four current fault classes and adds an isolated final-path witness, while removing five collected cases. The new fixture and assertions may offset any code reduction, and mode-by-fault interactions remain unproved. A six-case cut dropping the mode-change case would lose that metadata witness. No elapsed or net code saving is measured, and the probes were not a repository suite, Run, CI, or site execution. Keep A01-113's directory-enumeration and unstable-text-reader questions separate.

### A01-452 — Rendered HTML remote-resource branch adds only a diagnostic

For each active resource attribute, the inspector first checks `REMOTE_URI_RE` and then refuses values other than `data:`, fragments, or empty strings (`src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/validation.py:198-211,303-315`; `src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/models.py:25-45`). The changed text was the per-resource message, from `uses remote resource` to `is not embedded`. This supports the predicate reasoning but is not a full report, browser, or transaction run. The existing active-markup test asserts only the generic `active resources` header, not this wording (`tests/reporting/test_report.py:480-509`).

Staged/final rendering and retained transaction validation use the inspector (`src/emrys/reporting/_run_report/publication.py:153-180`; `src/emrys/reporting/transaction_validation.py:525-550`). The ratified reporting decision requires future changes to retain error messages (`docs/design/decisions/execution-evidence-and-reporting.md:186-192`), but its scope for this HTML-resource diagnostic is not explicit. Resolve that promise before treating the six-line reduction as behavior preserving; if the message is covered, an approved revision and independent replacement oracle are required. No tracked test pins this particular message. Preserve the generic resource refusal, separate active-URI/event/CSS guards, template-source remote check, and both publication and retained admission. ### A01-468 — Late VCF meta-information is accepted as a required header definition

The [VCF v4.2 specification](https://github.com/samtools/hts-specs/blob/master/VCFv4.2.tex) describes meta-information lines, then a column header, then data lines. The direct Step 07 reader skips every `##` line wherever it appears (`src/emrys/libraries/validation/mpileup.py:156-175`); the owner validator uses that sample/count projection (`src/emrys/stages/partitioned_cohort_mpileup/validator.py:120-201`). Reporting's VCF inspector collects `##FORMAT` and `##INFO` IDs before it distinguishes `#CHROM` and data lines, even if those declarations occur after data (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/_text_genomic.py:15-77`). Step 07 reconciliation then checks only the collected required-ID sets, sample order, and receipt counts (`src/emrys/reporting/_artifact_index/reconcile_native.py:204-220,257-265`). Moving only the `SP` declaration from the fixture's header to after its one record would leave that particular required-ID and count comparison satisfied (`tests/reporting/fixtures/artifact_adapters_v1/build_fixture.py:854-870`). A01-332 is different: it concerns a second `#CHROM` line, which reporting currently refuses.

A tiny isolated probe executed the pinned `inspect_vcf` and `iter_text_lines` function bodies with their source imports supplied directly, plus the importable direct `read_vcf`. For a one-record normal VCF and the same VCF with its only `SP` declaration moved after the record, both readers returned one record; reporting returned the same `SP` ID set. That confirms parser-level acceptance, not a complete Step 07 report, artifact transaction, native bcftools acceptance, or supported Run. The full reporting fixture also has a Step 08 VCF digest that would become stale after this mutation, so a whole-manifest failure would not isolate the Step 07 header-order fault.

Pin one owner-report and one artifact-index case that moves only the `SP` declaration after `#CHROM` or a data row, then require causal header-order refusal at the direct VCF/Step 07 boundary. Keep header-only VCF acceptance and the existing missing-definition, duplicate-`#CHROM`, and record-shape defenses. Any proposal to share a parser must replace both callers with equivalent accepted-byte and diagnostic behavior before retiring either check.

This scan identifies owner-specific policies; it does not justify a shared blanket guard or clear every unprobed alias.

### A01-478 — Step 06 direct report accepts aliased mechanical orientations

The grouped `emrys validate mechanical-orientation` route accepts separate FWD_like and REV_like BAM/BAI paths plus a counts TSV (`src/emrys/stages/mechanical_orientation/CONTRACT.md:59-83`; `src/emrys/stages/mechanical_orientation/validator.py:33-41`). The owner snapshots five path roles, checks BAM/BAI signatures pair by pair, and reconciles each orientation against the counts table, but never compares the two orientation file identities (`src/emrys/stages/mechanical_orientation/validator.py:44-130`). Counts are not recounted from BAM records by this direct validator, as the contract states (`src/emrys/stages/mechanical_orientation/CONTRACT.md:75-80`).

In tiny disposable fixtures, the exact pinned `validate_from_args(..., execute=True)` returned zero and published five passing rows for a normal five-file baseline, a case reusing the FWD BAM/BAI paths as REV arguments, and a case with separate hard-linked REV paths. Each alias case had only three `(device, inode)` identities among the five declared roles. Shared `snapshots` loses same-path duplicate keys but retains separate hardlink keys without testing physical distinctness (`src/emrys/libraries/validation/inputs.py:18-36,260-264`). Existing direct tests pin passing bytes and bad-container statuses but have no orientation-alias negative (`tests/stages/mechanical_orientation/test_validate_step_06_orientation_outputs.py:143-207`).

Require distinct FWD/REV BAM identities and distinct FWD/REV index identities at this owner boundary, with controlled exit 2 and no report; keep the normal positive and both alias variants. Run materialization names separate adapters, and Task refuses duplicate declared mutable pathnames (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/materialization.py:478-509`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/task.py:463-486`). That does not demonstrate physical hardlink refusal in a full Run. Preserve native producer status, BAM/BAI signature checks, independent counts and arithmetic, report roster, and Task all-pass admission (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/task.py:2763-2780`). This is a direct owner publication reproduction, not native samtools, full Task/Run, CI, Slurm, or strand biology.

At this owner boundary, require different `(device, inode)` identities for the two VCF roles, then pin same-path and hardlink negatives with controlled exit 2 and no report. Run materialization chooses two named VCF paths and Task rejects duplicate declared mutable pathnames (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/materialization.py:688-694`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/task.py:463-486`); neither source trace proves that Task refuses hard-linked native outputs. This is an exact direct-owner publication result, not a native bcftools, full Task/Run, CI, or Slurm result.

### A01-480 — Step 08 direct report admits its sites TSV as annotation GTF

The supported grouped `emrys validate cohort-candidate-preprocessing` route accepts a declared annotation GTF separately from three Step 08 TSV outputs (`src/emrys/stages/cohort_candidate_preprocessing/CONTRACT.md:105-132`). A disposable fixture built from the exact owner test helper produced a baseline five-row passing report. After the fixture receipts were updated to truthfully carry the admitted annotation path and hash, both `annotation_gtf=sites` at one pathname and separate hard-linked annotation/sites paths returned zero and published five `pass` rows from exact `validate_from_args(..., execute=True)`. Both alias cases had five physical identities for six declared roles, versus six in the baseline. Decide whether this direct owner route promises physically distinct annotation input and sites output; if so, pin same-path and hardlink refusals with a controlled exit and no report while retaining the five-row roster and receipt reconciliation. Run materialization supplies an external GTF and distinct output names, and Task rejects lexical input/output aliasing (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/materialization.py:757-815`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/task.py:463-486`). Task also rechecks input snapshots before and after native-output publication, which would refuse changed GTF bytes; its snapshots compare path, size, and hash rather than inode (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/task.py:573-592,2712-2725,2788-2790`). This probe did not show Task rejecting a preexisting hardlink or R producing a sites TSV from a TSV used as GTF. It used direct Python owner publication and intentionally synthetic upstream bytes, not native R, a full Run, CI, Slurm, or annotation biology.

### A01-481 — Managed golden-path clone integrity can become a no-op under source tests

The managed golden-path job finishes its native containment checks, then conditionally records all tracked and untracked changes in the clean clone and refuses a nonempty status file (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:851-858`). This is a distinct no-write check on the hosted journey's clean-clone source tree; the evidence upload and the earlier Doctor/Run checks do not replace it. The workflow-source test checks that the named integrity step follows the borrower and native-containment steps, but does not inspect that step's command or refusal (`tests/test_ci_workflow.py:439-445,576-598`).

An in-memory workflow copy replaced only that step body with valid shell `:` while keeping its name, condition, and order. YAML parsing still found all thirteen jobs and the tested order predicates remained true, although a changed clean clone would now leave the job green. Require a source oracle for the chosen clone and evidence paths, `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all`, the nonempty-status refusal, and the success-conditioned step. Preserve the hosted check itself, its evidence upload, and separate public Run/source-integrity tests. This is a workflow-source mutant result, not a hosted CI execution, an observed clone mutation, or permission to retire a gate.

### A01-482 — Storage cleanup tests omit two post-unlink states

After publishing a final direct or two-phase receipt, both routes call `_cleanup_probe` on each private probe directory (`src/emrys/evidence/storage_inventory/qualification.py:682-685,718-722`). The helper checks the four-member roster, unlinks each regular member, removes the emptied directory, then fsyncs its parent (`:628-637`). The current cleanup matrix injects first/second-probe errors before that helper and one error during the second member unlink (`tests/evidence/storage_inventory/test_storage_inventory.py:513-559`). Its retained-state assertions therefore do not isolate an empty probe directory after `rmdir` refusal or an absent probe directory after a failed parent fsync.

Exact `_cleanup_probe` probes in disposable directories injected `Path.rmdir` failure after all four unlinks and, separately, parent `_fsync_directory` failure after directory removal. The first left an empty probe directory; the second left none. In both cases the caller has already published the final receipt, whose authority remains separate from cleanup success (`src/emrys/evidence/storage_inventory/README.md:17-23`). These are two distinct recovery evidence states, not false qualification success, and A01-352 separately covers the manual debug command's raw `OSError` boundary.

Add a focused late-cleanup fault for each state with exact residual path/member assertions and unchanged final receipt bytes/admission. Preserve the earlier file-unlink and second-probe loop cases; do not reduce the current Cartesian matrix before its route-specific losses and any replacement costs are measured. The probes ran only the helper with disposable files, not full direct/final qualification, Doctor, CI, Slurm, or institutional storage.

## Protections to preserve during the next pass

The initial review found no basis for blanket retirement of independent numerical oracles, literal headers and check rosters, transaction and recovery fault tests, coverage baselines, installed-wheel smoke, guarded R and native-runtime checks, or disposable Slurm evidence. Similar test names across owners do not establish equivalent inputs or faults. Coverage measures Python execution, not scientific correctness or independent expectations.

The documentation gate's 19 fixed filenames preserve assigned reader and authority routes (`scripts/documentation/validate_structure.py:14-34`; `docs/README.md:8-29`). Link validation catches a missing destination only while an inbound link remains; deleting a page and its links together would evade that check (`scripts/documentation/validate_structure.py:164-196`). The fixed-name check therefore has a distinct maintenance fault, and the H1 check catches a present but headingless canonical page (`:199-206`). Retain both. The parser accepts any nonempty H1 anywhere, regardless of title or position (`:120-126`; `tests/documentation/test_validate_structure.py:158-176`); the guide's phrase "first headings" could imply a required opening heading, while the gate checks for an H1 anywhere (`scripts/documentation/README.md:3-6`). No fixed-title or first-line gate has a demonstrated need. A01-125/126/175 concern test exits, snapshot scope, and source-location admission rather than reasons to remove the named-page or H1 defenses.

An apparently duplicated Step 08 API check needs caution: its SHA-256 fingerprint includes the `Table` fields and `ContractError` ancestry, but the following explicit literal assertions protect those two invariants if someone deliberately rebaselines the opaque digest (`tests/contracts/scientific_evidence/test_step08.py:195-240`). The separate `__all__` roster protects export membership (`:242-270`); neither is a whole-test retirement. Similarly, missing `genome_chr_bin_nbits` remains an admitted current Project form (`src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/CONTRACT.md:129-134`; `tests/contracts/orchestration/test_orchestration_contracts.py:527-539`), and old-looking submission tests protect retained-request diagnostics (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_submission_inspection.py:544-563`; `tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_slurm_submission.py:1173-1204`). Historical names alone are not grounds for deletion. The seventeen-name source/caller disposition above found no whole test obsolete by name. A01-13 remains a conditional private-API absence retirement; A01-375 is a masked former-command sentinel, while A01-431/432 identify two current fixtures whose assertions miss the intended public boundary. None is a blanket test-removal decision.

The ingestion owner pass found no whole-test retirement: standalone manifest and FASTQ commands remain supported advisory routes, and their malformed inputs, optional file checks, prefix ceiling, decompression, and no-write assertions protect different decisions (`src/emrys/ingestion/sample_manifest_admission/validator.py:37-60,64-190`; `src/emrys/ingestion/sample_manifest_admission/check_fastq_pairs.sh:39-57,91-170`; `tests/ingestion/sample_manifest_admission/test_validate_manifest.py:48-263`; `tests/ingestion/sample_manifest_admission/test_check_fastq_pairs.py:85-346`). The ten packaged R namespace probes protect selected-library and version admission (`src/emrys/resources/runtime/runtime_policy.tsv:18-27`; `src/emrys/orchestration/run_coordinator/doctor.py:586-613`); this source pass found no basis to retire them. These are source and test dispositions, not local R or Viking qualification.

The workflow's literal processing-owner/rule/scope fence (`src/emrys/workflow/Snakefile:157-184`) and the profile-to-Stage Map/artifact-template tests (`tests/orchestration/run_coordinator/test_profile.py:271-306`) protect different graph representations. Real Snakemake fixtures use test-owned no-science commands, so their scheduling proof remains distinct from scientific results. R restoration runs only in explicit operator mode (`src/emrys/.Rprofile:76-125`; `src/emrys/resources/runtime/restore_r_environment.R:5-68`); guarded computation selects an existing library (`src/emrys/.Rprofile:27-75`). Preserve both mode boundaries and do not promote local restoration checks to Viking qualification.
